LR: Linear Regression, Huber: Huber Regression, LASSO(L1): LASSO Regression, Ridge(L2): Ridge Regression, KNN: K-Nearest Neighbour, DT: Decision Tree, AdaBoost: Adaptive Boosting, XGBoost: Extreme Gradient Boosting, RF: Random Forest, SVM: Support Vector Machines. 5.1.5.2 Feature selection Pre-Selected Features and Features Elimination Feature selection was performed in multiple steps. As shown in Figure 5-7, the first step is selecting features with missing ratio equal or less than 50%. Such features were used in preliminary model selection. Then, the artificial contrasts with ensembles (ACE) method was used for the selection of the key features from the features with a missing ratio below 50%. ACE is unsupervised and does not require a pre-selected number of features or pre-determined stopping criteria. It works by first estimating feature importance using an algorithm of ensemble of trees (RF was used). Then, for each feature in the dataset, an artificial random variable (called “artificial contrast variable”) is created from the same distribution as its corresponding feature but is independent of the target. A feature is eliminated if it has lower importance, that is artificial contrast (Tuv et al. 2006). Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 41 Figure 5-7. Feature Selection Method. Incremental Learning Following the ACE step, an incremental learning method (a modified Wrapper Dominating Hybrid Sequential Forward Floating Search) was used. In this method, features were added to the dataset in a sequential manner. Every time a feature is added, model performance is evaluated. If improved, permutation feature importance is calculated and the feature with least importance is dropped. If performance improved, this feature is dropped, and permutation feature importance is determined again. This process is repeated until the performance is not improving. If performance did not improve by dropping features, the added feature is selected without dropping any features. The incremental learning process for one of the iterations is shown in Figure 5-8. This process continues until the samples to features ratio (S/F ratio) is less than 10.
